en: The Ritual Manual for the Northern Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa Following the Army to Protect the Dharma,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daixingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa of Great Wisdom and Broad Intelligence, Bukong,
who was a Special Advancement and Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, Prince Nanda held a halberd in his hand and,
looking in the four directions with malevolent eyes, addressed the Buddha, saying:
I am the third prince of Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King of the North, and the grandson of his second son.
My grandfather, the Heavenly King,
and my uncle Nātha together [visit] three times every day.
He addressed the Buddha, saying,
"I shall protect and uphold the Buddha-dharma,
desiring to restrain and bind those who are evil or who give rise to unwholesome thoughts."
Day and night, I protect kings, ministers, and the hundred officials;
yet there are those among them who conspire together to kill,
strike down, or oppress others.
"We, the Nāgas, shall pierce their eyes and their hearts with vajra-staffs.
If anyone—whether a bhikṣu, bhikṣuṇī, upāsaka, or upāsikā—gives rise to unwholesome thoughts or murderous intent toward them."
He also struck his head with a vajra-club.
At that time, Vaiśravaṇa’s son, Nanda, addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One, ...”
For the sake of future sentient beings who are unwholesome,
so that they may be subdued, restrained, bound, and entirely dispersed,
and also for the sake of protecting and upholding the national borders.
"I shall now proclaim the mantra for subduing the turbulence of one's own mind.
May the World-Honored One grant me his permission.
"Excellent, excellent, Nanda Deva King! You may speak these words of the Buddha."
For the purpose of subduing all kings, ministers, and officials who commit acts of slaughter and oppression,
as well as those who act in opposition to the Dharma and the Buddha,
you may, for the sake of their subjugation, speak the mantra according to your will. It is as follows:
Oṃ dīśāna vaiśravaṇa-maṇaya mahārājāya yakṣādhipataye namo bhagavate mātaravate svāhā. If a practitioner upholds this mantra...
First, one must paint the image.
Among the pigments, no glue whatsoever may be mixed.
On a white cotton cloth (*karpāsa*), paint the deity Vaiśravaṇa and his grandson, the celestial being Nārāyaṇa, adorned with the seven precious jewels.
The left hand causes [the deity] to grasp the mouth and teeth;
the right hand is placed above the waist, causing [him] to grasp a three-pronged spear.
Beneath the feet of this deity stands a yakṣī in a seated posture.
It appears dark blue-black with a slight reddish tint.
When reciting this mantra,
one should choose a clean site and ensure it is free from filth and impurities.
One should make offerings of various flowers and incense.
The practitioner’s upper and lower garments must both be clean.
When entering the latrine, one should protect the body.
Beginning on the fifteenth night of the dark fortnight,
recite the mantra thirty thousand times before the image. Once this is completed,
take fragrant mud and make offerings to the honored image.
If there are those who act in opposition or rebellion against the king, ministers,
or officials, and unwholesome intentions arise,
perform homa with pine needles.
Within seven days,
Vajratiṣya stated that one should strike the head and heart [of the offender] with a vajra-mallet.
If there be any bhikṣu or bhikṣuṇī who commits this offense, [they shall suffer accordingly].
Perform a homa sacrifice using *kaṭuka* wood;
within seven days, [the offense] will be extinguished.
Furthermore, there is another method for those who have offended against a king.
Write the name of Śatru upon a piece of khadira wood;
repeatedly cause it to enter and exit within a triangular fire while reciting the aforementioned mantra aloud and visualizing Śatru in one's mind.
Furthermore, there is a method for subduing pūtanas and all kingly ghosts who come to seek an opportunity [to harm].
If one performs a homa with vajra wood,
[the enemy] will be utterly destroyed within no more than seven days.
Furthermore, when unwholesome enemies or bandits come to assault and kill [one], [this rite shall be performed].
Recite the aforementioned mantra seven times while forming the *mudrā* with the mind; [the spirits] will be naturally extinguished and will not dare to come.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subjugate an enemy or a violent and wicked person, perform a *homa* sacrifice using *kṛtavedhana* wood.
Furthermore, extract the juice from bitter wood and mix it with yellow earth to fashion the form of a śatru.
On its chest, write the person's name and seven times the word "śatru."
If one casts oneself into fire for seven days,
reciting the mantra repeatedly and forming the mudrā, there is no doubt that it will be extinguished.
Furthermore, there is another method for the four classes of followers.
If one gives rise to unwholesome thoughts toward the seven treasures,
or fails to honor parents, brothers, sisters, and the six classes of kinsmen,
one should perform a homa ritual using *gmelina arborea* wood according to the dharma.
All precious wealth will come of its own accord.
Furthermore, according to the ritual method, one should perform homa with *śrīparṇī* wood for one's wife, children, servants, vehicles, and the six types of domestic animals.
All six types of domestic animals will come of their own accord.
Furthermore, if one wishes to prevail over all people and malicious enemies,
one should fashion a three-pronged spear from pine wood.
Repeatedly strike the base of the altar.
On the base of that altar, arrange three figures of the *dhūru* and repeatedly strike them,
repeatedly severing [the bonds].
Furthermore, as for the gate of the Asura cave,
one should strike it with a trident;
it shall open of its own accord.
Furthermore, there is a method: by performing *homa* with lime mixed with *mṛttikā*, one will lead forty thousand celestial beings as offerings;
the enemy's national troops will surely come [to surrender].
As well as the armies of other nations,
were all simultaneously annihilated.
As for the "Mind Seal":
With the two hands bound within, the two *sūnyatā* (emptiness) fingers emerge; this is used for all matters of good and evil.
Formerly, when the five kingdoms were in great turmoil...
There are eight months during which the practice of many dharmas yields no results;
however, by performing this dharma, one subdues the five kingdoms and their fifty thousand armies, ensuring one's own safety.
Therefore, this is called the "Dharma for Protecting Armies."
The Ritual Manual for Vaiśravaṇa Deity Following the Army to Protect the Dharma.
